steps.rationale: A long-lived vendor API key with no MFA and no IP allow-list is replayed from the compromised vendor host.
The machine identity still carries a payment_write scope left over from a migration, so no escalation is needed.
Same entry hop: the static vendor API key.
Refund issuance is a legitimate business function the vendor uses daily, so abuse at scale blends in.

phases.detail: Static API key replayed from the compromised vendor host. No MFA challenge, no IP allow-list, so the first request succeeds and looks identical to normal traffic.
Enumerate scopes on vendor-svc-account via the IdP token introspection endpoint. payment_write appears alongside the expected refund_write.
Reuse the over-scoped token against payments-core. No escalation needed: the permission is already granted.
Structured transfers under per-transaction review thresholds until anomaly detection pages the SOC.
Refunds issued to attacker-controlled cards through a legitimate business function until the refund anomaly alert fires.

reasoning.title: Identify the entry point
reasoning.thought: vendor-portal is the only node marked external with an allowed outbound edge (e1). partner-sftp is external but its only edge (e8) is denied, a red herring.

reasoning.title: Name the first technique
reasoning.thought: A static api_key_auth on a machine identity with no second factor is T1078.004 (Valid Accounts: Cloud). Bypass probability 1.0 in config agrees: the control is effectively absent.

reasoning.title: Choose the branch
reasoning.thought: From vendor-svc-account, e2 and e3 are allowed; e4 (treasury-ledger) is denied so I did not follow it. Both e2 and e3 lead to financial nodes, so the path forks.

reasoning.title: Estimate the detection window
reasoning.thought: I estimated about 24h undetected on payments-core based on typical anomaly-rule tuning for payment APIs.

reasoning.title: Estimate losses
reasoning.thought: Assuming the attacker structures transfers below review thresholds, I estimate $2.4M to $3.1M movable across both systems before containment.

reasoning.title: Consider lateral extension
reasoning.thought: From payments-core, e5 gives db_write on core-ledger-db, which could allow ledger tampering to hide the transfers.

analysis.narrative: A compromised vendor integration reaches the payment estate in {hops} without breaking a single control. The vendor service account still carries a payment_write scope it no longer needs; against a mean time to detect of {mttd} on payments-core, an attacker can move up to {exposure} before anyone is paged, and hold {disruption} of critical payment processing at risk. The refund path is legitimate and stays. Revoking the one permission nobody uses removes {avoided} of that exposure.
